item.title: Recent Advances in Optimization and Decision Making under Uncertainty: Theory and Algorithms
item.content:encoded:
Abdel Lisser, Paris-Saclay University

Jia Liu, Xi'an Jiaotong University

Francesca Maggioni, University of Bergamo

S. K. Neogy, Indian Statistical Institute

Vikas Vikram Singh, Indian Institute of Technology Delhi

This special issue brings together recent advances in optimization and decision-making under uncertainty, focusing on theoretical contributions that strengthen the mathematical foundations and algorithmic techniques in operations research. The scope encompasses developments in stochastic, robust, and distributionally robust optimization, game theory, sequential decision-making, and learning-based methods that have expanded modern operations research's applicability.

The special issue welcomes original research presenting new optimization models, theoretical results, computational methodologies, and convergence analyses. While organized alongside ICORSI 2026 held at Indian Institute of Technology Delhi, the issue is open to all researchers in these areas regardless of conference participation.

Appel publié par Annals of Operations Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

  • Mathematical programming
  • Convex, nonconvex, and mixed-integer optimization
  • Stochastic, robust, and distributionally robust optimization
  • Chance-constrained optimization
  • Variational inequalities and equilibrium problems
  • Game theory and multi-agent optimization
  • Markov decision processes and stochastic games
  • Reinforcement learning for sequential decision making
  • Online and data-driven optimization
  • Optimization under risk measures
  • Bayesian optimization
  • Black-box optimization

  • March 31, 2028: Submission deadline

item.title: Advanced Machine Learning for System Reliability Management
item.content:encoded:
Yan-Fu Li, Tsinghua University

Hoang Pham, Rutgers University

Xu-Feng Zhao, Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

Industrial systems produce vast sensor-generated datasets that strain computational resources. Advanced machine learning techniques including transfer learning, federated learning, quantum machine learning, and reinforcement learning provide scalable solutions for handling large data volumes and enabling informed decision-making. Recent applications of these techniques to system reliability management encompass fault diagnosis, health assessment, remaining useful life prediction, degradation analysis, and maintenance optimization. This special issue seeks original research papers, reviews, and case studies exploring these emerging applications.

Appel publié par Annals of Operations Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Deep learning for anomaly detection and/or fault detection
  • Machine learning-enhanced maintenance optimization
  • Federated learning for system monitoring and predictive maintenance
  • Reinforcement learning for maintenance decision making
  • Transfer learning for cross-domain maintenance
  • Generative models for synthetic data generation for predictive maintenance
  • Self-supervised learning for unlabeled data for fault detection
  • Large models for fault detection and/or diagnosis
  • Generative models for reliability testing
  • Meta-heuristics for large-scale reliability design optimization

Timeline

  • September 30, 2026: Submission deadline

item.title: Advances in Quantitative Finance and Risk Modeling
item.content:encoded:
This special issue in the Annals of Operations Research invites high-quality research contributions in quantitative finance, insurance, and risk modeling. While connected to the Workshop on Quantitative Finance 2026 held in Bergamo, Italy, submissions are welcome from all researchers in the field, not just workshop participants.

The issue seeks rigorous methodological work that advances both theoretical understanding and practical applications in quantitative finance. Topics range from risk measurement and portfolio optimization to emerging areas such as machine learning applications, behavioral models, and climate-related financial risks.

item.title: Advances in Reliability and Statistical Computing for Intelligent Systems
item.content:encoded:
This special issue addresses advances in reliability and statistical computing for intelligent systems, reflecting the significant developments in AI and machine learning applications. The call seeks research that combines theoretical rigor with practical relevance, particularly focusing on how intelligent systems can provide reliable and timely responses in real-world applications across service industries and everyday use.

The special issue welcomes papers on new theoretical research and computational methods that advance the field. Preference is given to contributions demonstrating practical applications over purely theoretical work, with industrial case studies especially valued across domains such as robotics, medical care, education, surveillance, and intelligent transportation systems.

item.title: Climate Transition and Operational Risk Modelling: Implications for Supply Chains and Financial Decision-Making
item.content:encoded:
This special issue addresses how climate-related risks disrupt interconnected financial and economic systems during the transition to a low-carbon economy. The challenge lies in modeling how transition risks affect firms and supply chains, particularly carbon-intensive sectors, and understanding risk transmission across economic systems.

Firms face competing pressures to decarbonize while maintaining profitability and competitiveness. Significant vulnerabilities emerge through supply chain interdependencies, where disruptions propagate and amplify operational risks. The call seeks integrated modeling approaches that capture emissions, disruptions, and risks across supply chain tiers using operations research methods.

The issue welcomes applied and methodological studies employing stochastic optimization, machine learning, and other advanced techniques to examine how financial institutions manage uncertainty in portfolio allocation and risk management under climate transition scenarios.

item.title: Collaborative Intelligence in Operations Research: Models, Methods, and Applications
item.content:encoded:
Olga Battaïa, Kedge Business School

Yasser Dessouky, San Jose State University

Reza Zanjirani Farahani, Paris School of Business

Masood Fathi, University of Skövde

Madjid Tavana, La Salle University

Modern operations research faces challenges in dynamic and uncertain environments where traditional methodologies struggle. This special issue focuses on Collaborative Intelligence—integrating human expertise, artificial intelligence, and distributed problem-solving to enhance adaptability and efficiency in complex operations through multi-agent coordination, human-AI collaboration, and machine learning.

The special issue seeks research bridging autonomous AI systems and human decision-makers by combining computational power with human intuition and ethical reasoning. Contributions should address how collaborative approaches improve system resilience, handle uncertainty, and increase trust in AI-driven systems through theoretical advancements and computational methods that extend operations research to adaptive and multi-agent frameworks.

Researchers are invited to submit original contributions involving innovative mathematical models, algorithms, and practical applications demonstrating how collaborative intelligence enhances decision-making in complex operational environments, balancing theoretical rigor with practical relevance.

item.title: Contextual Optimization with Side Information: Theory, Methodology, and Applications
item.content:encoded:
Modern operations research increasingly relies on contextual information to enhance decision-making in uncertain environments. This special issue focuses on the integration of side information—such as demand patterns, user behaviors, and market conditions—into optimization models to achieve more adaptive and data-driven policies. The field spans contextual stochastic optimization, distributionally robust optimization with covariates, decision-focused learning, and online optimization frameworks.

Real-world applications present significant challenges including high-dimensional data, noisy observations, distribution shifts, computational constraints, and the need to balance predictive accuracy with operational performance. The special issue seeks high-quality contributions that develop novel theories, algorithms, and applications combining optimization with machine learning, statistics, and data analytics to address these challenges systematically.

item.title: Data-Driven Reliability Modeling and Decision Support in Industrial Engineering Systems
item.content:encoded:
Industrial engineering systems such as manufacturing, supply chains, energy networks, and transportation require reliable operation to maintain efficiency and safety amid uncertainty and disruptions. Traditional reliability approaches have relied on probabilistic and stochastic analysis, but advances in sensing technology and data collection now enable data-driven reliability modeling that combines classical theory with machine learning and statistical methods. The field is increasingly focused on integrating reliability analysis into decision-making frameworks for maintenance planning, resource allocation, and system optimization.

This special issue invites original research papers addressing reliability modeling and decision support for industrial engineering systems using operations research, industrial engineering, and data-driven methods. Both theoretical contributions and practical applications are welcome, with emphasis on methodological rigor and real-world relevance.

item.title: Data Science
item.content:encoded:
Dries F. Benoit, Ghent University

Kristof Coussement, IÉSEG School of Management

Cem İyigün, Middle East Technical University

Asil Oztekin, University of Massachusetts Lowell

This special section seeks to publish research that bridges data science and operations research, emphasizing both theoretical advances and practical organizational applications. The focus extends beyond technical innovation to address how analytics creates measurable value within organizations and drives necessary organizational change.

The collection invites contributions exploring the intersection of OR and analytics across multiple dimensions: ethical and governance considerations in data usage, challenges of applying OR techniques to big data and distributed systems, organizational barriers to analytics adoption, data quality and validation methods for large datasets, and the role of visualization and soft OR techniques in supporting data-driven decision making.

Appel publié par Annals of Operations Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Ethics and governance issues in analytics: How should data be obtained? What are the ethical implications of using applications of analytics to influence behavior?
  • Big data and analytics: What are the limitations and applications of optimization and other OR techniques to large datasets? What are the challenges for applications of OR methods within distributed systems? What is the possibility that OR models could in fact be the producers of big data, e.g., large-scale simulation models? What new methods/models in response to big data, e.g., sentiment mining, can be adopted by OR?
  • Organizational issues in analytics adoption: What are the issues facing organizations trying to adopt analytics? What is the role of real-time applications of OR in organizations?
  • Data quality and analytics: What methods can be used for hypothesis testing and model validation in large datasets? How can unstructured data be used effectively in OR models? What is the role of multi-methodology in business analytics? What opportunities do open data present for the OR discipline?
  • Analytics and decision support: How can data visualization techniques be used across the breadth of OR? What role do problem structuring and "soft" OR techniques play in analytics and big data projects?

Timeline

item.title: Game Theoretical Models and Applications SING21
item.content:encoded:
This special issue seeks to advance research on game theory as a framework for understanding strategic interaction, cooperation, conflict, and decision-making in complex systems. The collection emphasizes recent theoretical developments and diverse applications, particularly focusing on interaction dynamics and collective decision-making through both theoretical and practical contributions.

The issue particularly welcomes expanded and revised versions of papers presented at the European Meeting on Game Theory 2026 (SING21), though other relevant submissions are also encouraged. All papers undergo rigorous peer review by guest editors, with accepted contributions published online before appearing in print.

item.title: Global Supply Chain Reconfiguration Under Tariff Uncertainty
item.content:encoded:
Jiaguo Liu, Dalian Maritime University

Hakan Yildiz, Wayne State University

Guoqing Zhang, University of Windsor

This special issue addresses the challenges facing global supply chains as tariff uncertainty and shifting trade policies reshape sourcing, manufacturing, logistics, and market access. The contemporary environment presents unprecedented complexity requiring new decision-making approaches beyond traditional tariff-related research.

The collection seeks high-quality contributions applying Operations Research and Artificial Intelligence methods to supply chain reconfiguration under trade policy uncertainty. The issue welcomes theoretical advances, methodological innovations, applied modeling studies, and practical insights, with particular emphasis on interdisciplinary work integrating OR, AI, supply chain management, and international economics with real-world applications.

item.title: Multiple Objective Programming and Goal Programming: Artificial Intelligence for Decision Making in Economic and Social Sciences
item.content:encoded:
This special issue focuses on the convergence of Multiple Objective Programming (MOP), Goal Programming (GP), and Artificial Intelligence (AI) for addressing complex decision-making problems in economic and social sciences. The issue welcomes substantially extended papers from the 16th International Conference on Multiple Objective Programming and Goal Programming (MOPGP'25, held 1–3 July 2025 in Varese, Italy), as well as original unpublished papers not presented at the conference.

The special issue explores how MOP provides structured evaluation of conflicting objectives, GP facilitates goal-setting for decision makers, and AI enhances decision models through data analytics and machine learning. It covers theoretical advances and practical applications spanning sustainable development, resource allocation, public policy, environmental economics, social welfare optimization, and various computational methods for multi-criteria decision analysis.

item.title: OR for Sustainability in Supply Chain Management
item.content:encoded:
Kannan Govindan, University of Southern Denmark

This special section addresses the integration of the UN's 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into operations research and supply chain management. Organizations worldwide need to align their strategies with sustainability objectives to address resource depletion, pollution, and poverty. The collection seeks research that applies advanced operations research methods—such as multi-attribute and multi-objective decision making—to analyze and implement SDGs within supply chain environments at macro and organizational levels.

The special section welcomes contributions exploring three main themes: stakeholder-driven policy and design for SDGs; innovative strategies and practices for implementing sustainable supply chain management; and monitoring supply chain governance with respect to SDG targets. Research should demonstrate how optimization models and algorithms can improve data-driven decision-making, promote resource conservation, and support transitions toward more sustainable futures while addressing economic, environmental, and societal dimensions of supply chains.

item.title: OR in Medicine and Health Care
item.content:encoded:
Eva K. Lee, Georgia Institute of Technology

Ariela Sofer, George Mason University

This special section showcases optimization and computational approaches applied to medical and biological challenges. It aims to bring together mathematical programming researchers and healthcare professionals to address complex decision problems in medicine, from medical devices to clinical data analysis.

The special section welcomes theoretical and methodological research on optimization models and algorithms, including continuous, integer, combinatorial, and stochastic methods, applied to healthcare and life sciences. Topics of interest span disease modeling, diagnosis, treatment planning, medical imaging, epidemiology, and molecular biology.
